The data and cleaning steps behind the [COVID-19 mortality dashboard](../viz-covid-deaths-mexico/index.html). The question was how many more people died in Mexico in 2020 than in an ordinary year, and how much of that the records attribute to COVID-19. Answering it meant putting three official sources on the same footing, and then looking at other causes of death that might be related.

## Sources

Death records come from SEED, Mexico's epidemiological death registry, which is published as OLAP cubes. The official COVID-19 data were downloaded from coronavirus.gob.mx on 8 August 2020. Population comes from CONAPO's projections for 1990–2030 and turns counts into rates.

## How it was put together

Tableau's Microsoft Analysis Services connector reads the SEED cubes, and each view is flattened into its own sheet of an Excel file. A Tableau Prep flow then merges the three sources, harmonises their categories and writes the extracts the dashboard reads. The repository keeps every step: raw inputs, the connector workbook, the Prep flow and the outputs.

## What you get

Tableau extracts (`.hyper`) of deaths by state from 1998 to 2020 and by municipality from 2010 to 2020; municipal deaths for 2019 and 2020 with their ICD cause-of-death codes; the official COVID-19 records for 2020; and population by state and municipality for the same periods. The dashboard workbook, `DefuncionesCOVID19-Mexico.twb`, is included.
